AI-MAX-MS0::U-AIMAX09.systemImpact: The feature cascade feeds aiReasoningDispatcher and is consumed by AICapabilityMaximizerEngine's recommendation path; a regression here double-applies an enhancement pass so downstream AI-WIRE-MS0 round-trip E2Es and ai-feature-recommend hook injections surface inflated or contradictory scores. AWARE-MS0::U-AWARE06 (feature recommendation injection) depends on a stable cascade ordering.
csDepth: Per-stage gating on a confidence threshold introduces a short-circuit branch — verify the cascade is idempotent under re-entry (a memoized stage must key on the full input hash, not a partial), or a stale memo silently skips a needed recompute.

Feature-importance re-ranking after each stage is O(n log n) per stage and O(stages·n log n) overall; if stage count grows the re-rank dominates — consider an incremental heap update instead of a full sort.

AI-MAX-MS0::U-AIMAX11.systemImpact: These skill commands are thin routers into aiReasoningDispatcher actions; if their frontmatter drifts from command-frontmatter.schema.json the skill-auto-loader and skill-auto-trigger hooks silently fail to surface them, so the reasoning capability becomes unreachable from the prompt surface even though the dispatcher action still works. Slash-command fidelity tests gate this.
csDepth: Reasoning-chain DAG traversal must detect cycles — a self-referential reasoning chain causes unbounded recursion; use an explicit visited-set with depth cap rather than relying on natural termination.
The command-to-dispatcher routing table is a hot lookup; a hash map keyed by command name is correct, but keep logic out of the command (R5 — code answers deterministic routing, not the model).

AI-MAX-MS0::U-AIMAX12.systemImpact: A protective PreToolUse hook sits in the fleet-wide hook chain ahead of the first tool call; if it throws or mis-blocks it stalls every chat, and if it silently passes a bad payload it lets a degraded AI-capability state propagate into AI-MAX-MS0 builds. It must be wired in settings.json (an on-disk-only hook never fires) and respect MINIMAL_ALLOWLIST so a hook profile cannot disable it.
csDepth: The exit-2 pipe-truncation hazard is Windows-specific: a non-zero exit closes the stdout pipe before the JSON block flushes, so the gate is silently bypassed — always exit 0 and signal block via stdout JSON.
Hook latency is on the critical path of every tool call; bound any file read (size cap before JSON.parse) and avoid synchronous network calls — a slow guard hook degrades the whole fleet.

AI-TRAINING-FIRST-MS0::U-AITRAIN-ACADEMY.systemImpact: CrossDisciplinaryDeepLearningEngine is PRISM's cross-domain synthesis entry point (15 scientific domains); a checkpoint that overfits the JM-DIE corpus poisons every consumer of prismCreativeReasoningEngine and the recommendAIFeatures path. Per the pre-revenue doctrine, all revenue milestones are gated behind this training pass landing correctly.
csDepth: A heterogeneous corpus (CAD + course + kernel) needs per-source feature normalization before the train/validation split — splitting raw then normalizing leaks validation statistics into training (the NN-GRAPH stratified-negative lesson).

Checkpoint serialization must embed training metadata (corpus fingerprint, split seed, epoch) so the U2 self-retrain lifecycle can decide promote/decline deterministically; an undated checkpoint cannot be drift-compared.

AI-TRAINING-FIRST-MS0::U-AITRAIN-ACADEMY.systemImpact: MITCourseDeepLearningEngine feeds the course-content-to-KnowledgeTip routing that the cad-engine knowledge_store auto-loads; a bad checkpoint degrades tribal-tip recommendations across /pdf-learn and /video-learn outputs. KNOWLEDGE-CONVERSION-MS0's Lane A/B/C router consumes the same corpus, so schema agreement matters.
csDepth: Corpus chunking choice (fixed-window vs semantic) determines feature granularity — fixed-window is O(n) and reproducible; semantic chunking risks non-determinism that breaks the regression oracle.
Probe the course-corpus JSON schemaVersion before ingest — the recurring schema-blindness bug is assuming totals.* vs top-level field placement without reading the file.

AI-TRAINING-FIRST-MS0::U-AITRAIN-CAM-CAM.systemImpact: CAMDeepLearningEngine's strategy predictions are consumed by camDispatcher toolpath selection; a checkpoint that memorizes JM-DIE answers ships wrong CAM strategy recommendations into the print-to-program pipeline, breaking DOMAIN-PIPELINE-MS0's TOOLPATH_GEN stage. The CAM orchestrator unit (sibling) wraps this engine.
csDepth: A k-NN similarity index over training examples is O(n) per query without an ANN structure — for a 76K corpus build a ball-tree / HNSW index or queries dominate inference latency.
CAM toolpath feature vectorization must be order-invariant where toolpath operations commute; encoding operation order into the vector causes the model to learn a spurious sequencing signal.

AI-TRAINING-FIRST-MS0::U-AITRAIN-CAM-CAM.systemImpact: The CAM orchestrator ensembles per-engine CAM deep-learning predictions; if a wrapped engine is missing it must fail loud, not silently drop a sub-model — a silent skip degrades the ensemble's accuracy invisibly and the DOMAIN-PIPELINE-MS0 orchestrator stage that depends on it ships wrong toolpaths with full confidence.
csDepth: Ensemble aggregation must define a tie/abstain policy — if sub-models disagree at equal weight, returning an arbitrary winner hides genuine uncertainty; surface it (R12).

Orchestrating multiple training stages introduces a partial-failure mode: a crash on stage 3 of 5 leaves stages 1-2 checkpoints written — make stage writes atomic and resumable, not all-or-nothing in memory.

AI-TRAINING-FIRST-MS0::U-AITRAIN-CAM-FUS.systemImpact: FusionDeepLearningEngine is a ghost/unbuilt engine — it must be built before training, and once built it feeds Fusion360AIOrchestrationEngine and the CAD-automation Fusion bridge. The cad-fusion-training-ms0 wiki records that Fusion cloud is unreachable without Forge creds, so the corpus pivots to Inventor/STEP — this unit must use that same transferable B-rep corpus.
csDepth: Building a ghost engine first means running duplicationGuardEngine.mustCheckBeforeCreating — a 'ghost' flag is sometimes digest-staleness, the engine may already exist unwired.
.f3d feature extraction must handle the proprietary binary format gracefully; a parse failure on one file must not abort the whole corpus ingest — collect-and-continue with a logged skip count.

AI-TRAINING-FIRST-MS0::U-AITRAIN-CAM-HYP.systemImpact: HyperMillDeepLearningEngine (ghost) once built feeds hyperMILL strategy selection through camDispatcher and the hyperMILL automation bridge (CAD-AUTOMATION-MS0::U-CAUT07). hyperMILL has 25 already-extracted assets — do not re-extract; the model should consume the existing function index.
csDepth: hyperMILL strategy feature vectorization shares structure with the generic CAM engine — extract a shared vectorizer to avoid two divergent feature spaces that the orchestrator cannot ensemble.
k-NN over a sparse strategy space risks empty neighborhoods for rare strategies; fall back to a class-prior rather than returning a nearest-but-irrelevant match.

AI-TRAINING-FIRST-MS0::U-AITRAIN-CAM-MAS.systemImpact: MastercamDeepLearningEngine (ghost) feeds Mastercam strategy selection consumed by camDispatcher and MastercamMultiAxisEngine. Mastercam has 45 already-extracted assets — the model trains on those, not a re-extraction. A bad checkpoint mis-routes the most-used CAM vendor's strategy.
csDepth: Softmax classification over strategy classes needs class-balanced sampling — a JM-DIE corpus heavily skewed toward a few strategies trains a model that always predicts the majority class with high softmax confidence.
Validate prediction accuracy with a stratified held-out set so each strategy class is represented in evaluation, not just the common ones.

AI-TRAINING-FIRST-MS0::U-AITRAIN-DATABAS.systemImpact: ToolDatabaseDeepLearningEngine (ghost) once built recommends tools consumed by speed/feed and CAM toolpath units; a checkpoint that overfits poisons tool selection across the print-to-program TOOLING_SELECT stage. The tool catalog is the ground-truth source — schema-probe it before embedding.
csDepth: Tool-record embedding must handle mixed categorical (material, coating) and continuous (diameter, flute count) features — one-hot the categoricals or the model treats nominal codes as ordinal.
Similarity search over the tool catalog is a nearest-neighbor query; for an updatable catalog choose an index that supports incremental insert, or every catalog update forces a full rebuild.

AI-TRAINING-FIRST-MS0::U-AITRAIN-LATHE-L.systemImpact: LatheDeepLearningEngine feeds turningDispatcher and the lathe studio pipeline; a regression mis-predicts lathe program parameters consumed by DOMAIN-PIPELINE-MS0's lathe FULL_PIPELINE. LatheDeepReasoningEngine (sibling) shares the lathe corpus, so feature-space agreement matters.
csDepth: Lathe-program feature extraction must canonicalize G-code dialect first (Okuma S[Vnn] vs Fanuc S-numeric) — the regex trap documented in PRISM regressions causes the model to learn dialect noise as signal.
Train/validation split should be by program (not by line) so a held-out program is wholly unseen — line-level splitting leaks the same program's structure into both sets.

AI-TRAINING-FIRST-MS0::U-AITRAIN-LATHE-L.systemImpact: LatheDeepLearningIntelligenceEngine (ghost) once built layers reasoning-chain inference over LatheDeepReasoningEngine; it is consumed by the lathe AGI master path. A ghost-build must dedup-check first — the intelligence-tier engine may overlap an existing reasoning engine.
csDepth: Reasoning-chain feature vectorization over variable-length chains needs a fixed-dimension encoding (pooling or attention) — padding to a max length wastes capacity and biases toward short chains.
k-NN similarity over training examples must define a distance metric appropriate to the embedding space — cosine for normalized embeddings, not Euclidean, or magnitude dominates.

AI-TRAINING-FIRST-MS0::U-AITRAIN-LATHE-L.systemImpact: LatheKinematicsDeepLearningEngine predictions feed the lathe kinematic-validity path; if the model invents kinematics rather than deferring to canonical FK/IK math, downstream collision and work-envelope checks accept physically impossible programs. Kinematics labels are safety-relevant ground truth.
csDepth: Forward/inverse kinematics ground-truth labelling must come from the deterministic InverseKinematicsSolverEngine — never let the trained model become the authority on kinematics; it is an accelerator over math, not a replacement.
IK can have multiple valid solutions (elbow-up/elbow-down); the labelling must pick a canonical branch consistently or the model trains on contradictory labels for identical inputs.

AI-TRAINING-FIRST-MS0::U-AITRAIN-LATHE-L.systemImpact: LatheMetaLearningEngine produces fast-adapting models for new lathe tasks; its meta-learned initialization feeds LatheDeepLearningEngine fine-tuning. If the task partition is wrong it learns a single-task model masquerading as a meta-learner — every downstream fast-adapt claim is then false.
csDepth: Meta-learning needs a distribution of tasks — partition the lathe corpus by material/operation/machine into distinct tasks; treating one dataset as one task collapses MAML to ordinary training.
MAML's inner/outer loop is second-order (gradient through a gradient); first-order approximation (FOMAML) is cheaper — choose explicitly and document the accuracy/cost tradeoff.

AI-TRAINING-FIRST-MS0::U-AITRAIN-LATHE-L.systemImpact: LatheSpeedFeedDeepLearningAdvisorEngine output feeds the lathe speed/feed advisory consumed by /auto-speed-feed-lathe and the SPEED_FEED pipeline stage; an ML prediction outside the Kienzle/Taylor physics envelope produces unsafe spindle/feed values that the SAFETY_VALIDATE stage must catch — but the advisor must self-clamp first.
csDepth: ML speed/feed output must be clamped to the canonical physics envelope post-prediction — the model is an interpolator within the safe region, never an extrapolator past it.
Speed/feed is a regression target with heteroscedastic noise (variance grows with cut depth) — a plain MSE loss underweights high-DOC error; consider a relative or quantile loss.

AI-TRAINING-FIRST-MS0::U-AITRAIN-MILL-FI.systemImpact: FiveAxisAIUltraIntelligenceEngine (ghost) once built feeds 5-axis tilt/collision advisory; its collision-avoidance predictions must DEFER to the deterministic collision engine, never override it — a model that overrides a deterministic safety check ships a crash. fiveAxisDispatcher consumers depend on this hierarchy.
csDepth: Collision-avoidance is a hard safety constraint, not a learned objective — the ML layer proposes tilt candidates, the deterministic WorkEnvelopeValidatorEngine vetoes; this two-tier design must be enforced structurally, not by convention.
5-axis collision feature representation is high-dimensional (tool + part + fixture geometry); dimensionality reduction risks discarding the exact feature that distinguishes a near-miss from a crash.

AI-TRAINING-FIRST-MS0::U-AITRAIN-MILL-FI.systemImpact: FiveAxisDeepLearningEngine (ghost) feeds 5-axis toolpath optimization through fiveAxisDispatcher; collision logic must stay deterministic — the model optimizes within the validated region only. Downstream the FiveAxis ultra-intelligence engine (sibling) ensembles this.
csDepth: 5-axis toolpath feature vectorization must encode the rotary-axis pair correctly (the rotation_order 2-char rotary-pair convention from PRISM regressions) — mislabeling A/B/C pairs trains the model on inconsistent kinematics.
Validation on held-out 5-axis programs must check no predicted toolpath enters a collision state — accuracy alone is insufficient for a safety-adjacent model.

AI-TRAINING-FIRST-MS0::U-AITRAIN-MILL-MI.systemImpact: MillDeepLearningEngine (ghost) feeds milling program prediction through millDispatcher and the mill studio; a ghost-build must dedup-check against MillingDeepReasoningEngine and MillingDeepIntegrationEngine first — the milling domain has dense engine coverage. DOMAIN-PIPELINE-MS0's mill FULL_PIPELINE consumes it.
csDepth: Milling-program feature extraction over a 76K corpus is the memory bottleneck — stream the corpus and accumulate features incrementally rather than loading all programs into memory.
Train/validation split by program with a fixed seed makes the regression oracle reproducible; an unseeded split makes accuracy non-comparable across runs.

AI-TRAINING-FIRST-MS0::U-AITRAIN-MILL-MI.systemImpact: MillingAIUltraIntelligenceEngine (ghost) is the top-tier milling intelligence consumed by the milling AGI master path; if it uses LoRA adapters, the AdaLoRARankAllocatorEngine and FederatedLoRAEngine govern rank — a mis-sized adapter underfits or wastes capacity, degrading every milling reasoning consumer.
csDepth: LoRA rank allocation is a capacity/cost tradeoff — too low underfits the milling-strategy manifold, too high erases the parameter-efficiency benefit; let AdaLoRARankAllocatorEngine decide rather than hardcoding rank.
Knowledge synthesis / ensemble fusion across sub-models needs a fusion weight that is itself validated — uniform averaging assumes equal sub-model competence, which is rarely true.

AI-TRAINING-FIRST-MS0::U-AITRAIN-MILL-MI.systemImpact: MillingMetaLearningEngine produces fast-adapting milling models; its meta-learned init feeds MillDeepLearningEngine fine-tuning and is referenced by the milling tribal-corpus bridge. A bad task partition collapses the meta-learner to single-task training, invalidating all fast-adapt claims downstream.
csDepth: Partition the milling corpus into distinct tasks (by material/feature/machine) — the meta-learner's value is fast adaptation to an UNSEEN task, so the held-out validation tasks must not overlap meta-training tasks.
MAML inner/outer loop second-order gradients are memory-heavy on a large corpus — batch task sampling and consider FOMAML to bound memory.

AI-TRAINING-FIRST-MS0::U-AITRAIN-MILL-VI.systemImpact: VirtualMachiningDeepLearningEngine (ghost) once built predicts machining-simulation outcomes consumed by the SIMULATE pipeline stage; predictions that diverge from real machining outcomes give operators false confidence at the pre-machine gate.
csDepth: Simulated predictions must be validated against REAL machining outcomes, not against the simulator that generated the training labels — a sim-to-sim loop just learns the simulator's biases.
Virtual-machining simulation feature extraction is high-dimensional spatiotemporal data; choose a representation (voxel grid vs feature summary) that the downstream model can consume without OOM.

AI-TRAINING-FIRST-MS0::U-AITRAIN-MISC-ME.systemImpact: MetaLearningOptimizerEngine is the shared meta-learning substrate referenced by every domain meta-learning unit (lathe, milling, post-processor) — a regression here propagates to all of them. It is the highest-leverage AI-training unit because it is a common dependency.
csDepth: The optimizer learns hyperparameters over a task distribution — validate that learned hyperparameters TRANSFER to unseen tasks, not just minimize loss on the training tasks (the overfit-to-task-set failure mode).
Gradient-based optimizer state (momentum, adaptive LR) must be serialized with the checkpoint so a resumed meta-training run does not silently restart the optimizer from cold.

AI-TRAINING-FIRST-MS0::U-AITRAIN-POST-CN.systemImpact: CNCControllerDeepLearningEngine (ghost) once built classifies controller dialects feeding the post-processor pipeline; a mis-classified dialect routes G-code through the wrong post-processor template, producing NC output the machine rejects. ppDispatcher and the master post-processor consume this.
csDepth: Controller-dialect classification over G/M-code grammar — extract grammar-level features (canned-cycle codes, address-word patterns), not raw text, or the model learns comment-style noise.
Controller families are imbalanced in any real corpus (Fanuc/Haas dominate); class-balance the training set or the model never learns rare dialects.

AI-TRAINING-FIRST-MS0::U-AITRAIN-POST-PO.systemImpact: PostProcessorDeepLearningEngine (ghost) feeds post-processor logic generation consumed by ppDispatcher and the POST_PROCESS pipeline stage; generated logic must be validated against rendered NC output — a model that produces plausible-but-wrong post logic ships broken NC programs.
csDepth: Validate generated post-processor logic by RENDERING it and parsing the NC output, not by string-similarity to a reference — the post-processor's correctness is in the rendered program, not the template text.
Post-processor template feature extraction must capture the template's control-flow structure (conditionals, blocks), not just token frequency.

AI-TRAINING-FIRST-MS0::U-AITRAIN-POST-PO.systemImpact: PostProcessorMetaLearningEngine produces fast-adapting post-processor models; its value is adapting to a NEW controller with few examples. The task partition is by controller family — if a held-out controller leaks into meta-training, the fast-adapt claim consumed by ppDispatcher is false.
csDepth: Partition the post-processor corpus by controller family as distinct meta-learning tasks — fast-adaptation must be validated on a controller family entirely held out of meta-training.
A new controller often has very few examples — the inner-loop adaptation must be stable in the few-shot regime; verify it does not diverge with a tiny support set.

AI-TRAINING-FIRST-MS0::U-AITRAIN-SPEEDFE.systemImpact: SpeedFeedDeepLearningEngine output feeds calcDispatcher speed/feed advisory and the SPEED_FEED pipeline stage across all domains; it is a cross-domain consumer, so a regression affects mill, lathe, and CAM pipelines. Output must be clamped to the canonical physics envelope (constants.ts kc1.1 values).
csDepth: Never inline kc1.1 / Kienzle / Taylor constants — import from constants.ts; the ML output is bounded by physics, and the bound's source of truth must be the canonical file (P=1800, M=2100, K=1100, N=700, S=2800, H=3200).
Feature extraction must key material on the ISO group, not free-text material name — a name-string feature fragments the same material across spelling variants.

AI-TRAINING-FIRST-MS0::U-AITRAIN-WIRE-EL.systemImpact: ElectrodeDeepLearningEngine feeds electrode-design recommendations through edmDispatcher consumed by ElectrodeDesignEngine and the WEDM/sinker EDM pipeline; predictions must respect EDM physics constants — a model that invents electrode geometry ships unmachinable electrode designs into APPW-MS8's sinker EDM bridge.
csDepth: Electrode-geometry feature extraction must encode the geometric envelope (overburn, spark gap) as physics-bounded features, not free parameters the model can extrapolate past.
EDM physics ground-truth labelling must come from canonical EDM constants — the WEDM domain has 62 engines; the trained model is an accelerator over that physics, never the authority.

AI-WIRE-MS0::U-AIW01.systemImpact: Wiring AI core engines to aiReasoningDispatcher makes them reachable from the MCP surface; an enum-only ghost-wire 100% fails in production and the stop_on_unwired_assets hook will block the Stop. Every AI-MAX-MS0 and AWARE-MS0 consumer that calls aiReasoningDispatcher actions depends on these wires being real executors.
csDepth: A wiring is incomplete unless the action is BOTH in the z.enum(ACTIONS) gate AND backed by an executor body — the ghost-wired-orphan class (enum entry + slimResponse but no executor) passes naive tests and 100%-fails live.
A MockMCPServer that bypasses the z.enum() SDK gate false-greens a missing-from-enum action — the round-trip E2E must drive the real dispatcher, not a mock.

AI-WIRE-MS0::U-AIW02.systemImpact: These schema definitions are the contract between the MCP boundary and the AI core engines; a schema that disagrees with the engine's actual input shape produces a silent runtime mismatch that U-AIW01's wiring then routes — schema drift here breaks every consumer downstream.
csDepth: Read the engine's actual input signature before authoring the Zod schema — a schema written from an assumed shape is the recurring schema-blindness bug; the engine source is the source of truth.
A discriminated union schema must have an exhaustive discriminant — a missing variant makes Zod reject a valid payload at runtime, not at type-check time.

AI-WIRE-MS0::U-AIW03.systemImpact: Wiring safety/guard engines to guardDispatcher makes the safety gates reachable; these are the engines AGISafetyContainmentEngine and BuildGuardChainEngine expose, so a wiring error that defaults to ALLOW silently disables a safety gate fleet-wide. Guard engines must fail closed.
csDepth: A guard wiring must fail closed — if the dispatcher cannot reach the guard engine the default decision is BLOCK, never silent ALLOW; a fail-open guard is worse than no guard because it gives false assurance.
Safety-gate guards are on the critical path of build operations — keep the guard's executor bounded and synchronous-fast, or it becomes a fleet-wide latency sink.

AI-WIRE-MS0::U-AIW03b.systemImpact: Guard-action schemas validate payloads before they reach a safety gate; a loose schema lets a malformed or hostile payload through to the guard engine, defeating U-AIW03's fail-closed wiring. This is the input-validation layer for the safety tier.
csDepth: Read each guard engine's real input shape before authoring the schema — a loose schema (z.any(), optional-everything) at a safety boundary is an unvalidated-input hole.
Schema validation of a safety-gate payload should reject unknown keys (strict mode), not silently strip them — a stripped key may be the one carrying the unsafe instruction.

AI-WIRE-MS0::U-AIW04.systemImpact: Wiring agent/cognitive engines to agentDispatcher makes autonomous-goal and cognitive capabilities reachable; AutonomousGoalSynthesisEngine and the agent layer are consumed by orchestration units. An enum-only wire ghost-fails and the stop_on_unwired_assets hook blocks the Stop.
csDepth: Each agent engine needs an enum entry plus a real executor body — verify with a round-trip E2E that drives the real dispatcher, not a mock that skips the enum gate.
Agent engines may have long-running invocations; the dispatcher contract should define a timeout and a cancellation path, or a wedged agent invocation blocks the dispatcher.

AI-WIRE-MS0::U-AIW04b.systemImpact: Agent-action schemas are the contract between the MCP boundary and the agent engines; schema drift produces a silent runtime mismatch that U-AIW04's wiring routes — the schema must match each agent engine's actual signature.
csDepth: Read each agent engine's actual signature before writing its schema — schema drift surfaces as a runtime contract mismatch, not a compile error.
Agent action input often nests structured goal/context objects — model these as explicit Zod object schemas with schemaVersion, not free-form records, so a version bump has a migration path.

AI-WIRE-MS0::U-AIW05.systemImpact: Wiring neural/deep-learning engines makes the trained models from AI-TRAINING-FIRST-MS0 reachable from the MCP surface — this unit is the bridge between the training milestone and any consumer; if the wires are ghosts the trained checkpoints are unreachable. Wire to every dispatcher that would naturally consume each engine.
csDepth: Per the WIRE-TO-ALL-SOURCES doctrine, a neural engine wires to its primary dispatcher AND every dispatcher that would naturally consume it — single-dispatcher wiring leaves the engine half-orphaned.
Verify each wire with a real round-trip E2E; a neural engine that loads a heavy checkpoint should lazy-load on first invocation so the dispatcher startup is not blocked.

AI-WIRE-MS0::U-AIW06.systemImpact: Wiring physics engines to BOTH calcDispatcher and vibrationPhysicsDispatcher (the WIRE-TO-ALL-SOURCES rule for physics) makes manufacturing physics reachable; physics engines are consumed by speed/feed, safety, and chatter units. A wiring layer that inlines a constant fragments the canonical-constants source of truth.
csDepth: Never inline physics constants in the wiring layer — import from constants.ts; the wiring is a router, not a place for kc1.1 values.
Physics engine tests must use real reference values and algebraic invariants — a toBeDefined() stub for a physics result is hook-rejected and proves nothing about the computed force/temperature.

AI-WIRE-MS0::U-AIW08.systemImpact: Wiring reasoning engines to aiReasoningDispatcher makes PRISMCreativeReasoningEngine's cross-domain synthesis reachable; AI-MAX-MS0 skill commands and the ai-feature-recommend hook depend on these actions resolving to real executors.
csDepth: Each reasoning engine needs an action-enum entry plus an executor body — a mock that bypasses the enum gate false-greens a missing action; the E2E must hit the real dispatcher.
Reasoning-engine invocations can be token-heavy; the dispatcher contract should expose a mode/effort parameter so callers can scope cost (R6 — token budgets are not advisory).

AI-WIRE-MS0::U-AIW09.systemImpact: Wiring learning engines to aiReasoningDispatcher makes MetaLearningOptimizerEngine and LearningCascadeEngine reachable; the AUTO-LEARNING-LOOP-MS0 milestone's auto-learning actions consume these wires, so a ghost-wire breaks the closed-loop learning pipeline.
csDepth: A mock MCP server that skips z.enum() will false-green a missing learning action — the round-trip E2E must exercise the real enum gate (the recurring MS0-false-green class).

Learning engines may carry mutable training state; the dispatcher invocation must be explicit about whether a call mutates the engine (train) or is read-only (infer), or concurrent calls race the state.

AI-WIRE-MS0::U-AIW07a.systemImpact: Comprehensive test coverage for all new AI-WIRE-MS0 actions is the regression oracle for the whole milestone; without real-value round-trip E2Es a ghost-wired action ships green. The scrutinize-before-stop 3-of-3 gate and stop_on_failing_tests hook depend on these tests being real.
csDepth: Tests must encode WHY the behavior matters with real reference values — toBeDefined() stubs are hook-rejected; a test that passes against a hardcoded return value verifies nothing (R9).
Round-trip E2E through every wired dispatcher (not only the primary one) is the WIRE-TO-ALL-SOURCES acceptance criterion — coverage of one dispatcher leaves the other wires unverified.

AI-WIRE-MS0::U-AIW07b.systemImpact: The doc + index refresh propagates the AI-WIRE-MS0 changes into the four doc surfaces and regenerates the master index; a stale index means subagent pre-search and master-index-precheck-inject miss the new actions, so future chats re-derive or duplicate them. This closes the milestone's awareness loop.
csDepth: Index regeneration must be idempotent — a non-idempotent rebuild that appends duplicates corrupts the master index; check existing entries before write.
Generated indexes must be written atomically (temp + rename) — a reader hitting a half-written index sees truncated JSON; the system-graph multi-writer race is the cautionary case.

APPW-MS8::U-APPW39.systemImpact: Execution-surface materialization maps routes to renderable L9 frontend pages; if a surface is claimed materialized but the route 404s, every APPW-MS8 sibling that links to it ships a dead link. /page-sweep preflight is the verification gate — coordination sync keeps the surface manifest consistent with what other chats have built.
csDepth: Verifying a surface is materialized means a real render check, not trusting the manifest — a manifest entry is an assertion, the rendered page is the evidence (R12 — 'feature works' is a lie if the page 404s).
Coordination state sync across surfaces is a concurrent-write hazard — two chats materializing surfaces simultaneously must use a lock or atomic merge, or one overwrites the other's manifest entry.

APPW-MS8::U-APPW40.systemImpact: The calculator design contract pins the input/output shape between the L9 calculator UI and calcDispatcher; if the contract is extracted from an assumed engine API rather than the real one, the shell surface and the engine disagree and the calculator UI renders wrong results. Downstream APPW-MS8 viewer units depend on this contract.
csDepth: Extract the shell surface from the REAL engine API signature — a contract written against an assumed shape is the schema-blindness bug at the UI/engine boundary.
The calculator contract must pin units and physics-constant provenance — a calculator that inlines a constant diverges from constants.ts and silently produces stale results.

APPW-MS8::U-APPW41B.systemImpact: The electrode macro/reference bridge activates the legacy electrode-macro archive without rewriting it; SinkerEDMElectrodeGeometryEngine and the sinker EDM pipeline consume the bridged macros. If the reference path does not resolve at activation the bridge silently serves no macros — verify the path before claiming activation.
csDepth: The bridge is an adapter over a legacy archive — wrap, do not rewrite (R8); a rewrite risks losing the macro semantics the legacy archive encodes.
Legacy archive activation should be lazy-load with a resolved-path check at activation time — a missing archive directory must fail loud, not return an empty macro set.

APPW-MS8::U-APPW43A.systemImpact: Viewer contract verification hardens the request/response shape between the L9 backplot viewer and the CAM/toolpath backend; a viewer that accepts malformed backplot results renders garbage or crashes. The api-contract-enforcer hook depends on the contract being precisely specified.
csDepth: Verify the viewer contract by parsing REAL backplot results and asserting concrete params — 'the response is defined' is not verification (R9/R12); assert the actual toolpath segment count, coordinates, etc.
Backplot result data structures can be large; the viewer must validate shape before deep traversal and bound memory — a malformed-but-huge payload is a DoS vector.

APPW-MS8::U-APPW44.systemImpact: Authoritative /page-sweep is the milestone's truth gate — a real headless-browser render check of every APPW-MS8 page plus benchmark reconciliation; it is the closeout verification for the whole APPW milestone. If it false-passes, dead pages and wrong benchmark numbers ship as 'done'.
csDepth: An authoritative page-sweep must drive a real browser render, not parse the route manifest — fail loud on any 404 or benchmark disagreement (R12 — silence is not success).
Benchmark truth reconciliation needs deterministic fixtures — a benchmark that varies run-to-run cannot be reconciled; pin the fixture and the comparison tolerance.

ARCH-MS2::U-ARCH01.systemImpact: The ARCH-MS2 coordinator sequences sibling units and closes the milestone; if it closes the milestone while a sibling's deliverable never shipped, MILESTONE_PROGRESS and BUILD_STATE record false completion — the silent-close-out-debt class. Downstream milestones that list ARCH-MS2 as a dependency then build on phantom foundations.
csDepth: Dependency ordering across sibling units is a topological sort — a cycle in the unit dependency graph makes the coordinator non-terminating; detect cycles explicitly.

Before closing, the coordinator must verify each unit's deliverable exists on disk AND its status is reconciled in MILESTONE_PROGRESS — file presence alone is not spec correctness (close-out-audit is advisory, human-verify).

ARCH-MS3::U-ARCH01.systemImpact: The ARCH-MS3 coordinator sequences ARCH-MS3 units and is itself a dependency of ARCH-MS4 (which references ms3); a premature close cascades a false-complete state forward into ARCH-MS4's coordinator, which then sequences against a foundation that may not exist.
csDepth: QA-state aggregation across units must define how a partial-pass aggregates — if one unit is in_progress the milestone is not complete; never average a pass/fail into a misleading 'mostly done'.
Topological dependency ordering must be recomputed if units are added mid-milestone — a cached order goes stale and sequences a new unit before its prerequisite.

ARCH-MS4::U-ARCH01.systemImpact: The ARCH-MS4 coordinator sequences ARCH-MS4 units and depends on ARCH-MS3's coordinator having genuinely closed; it is the terminal architecture-milestone coordinator, so its close declares the ARCH track done. A false close here misreports the entire architecture line as complete in ROADMAP-CONSOLIDATED.
csDepth: Verify dependency order and shipped deliverables — the silent-close-out-drift detector exists because pre-tagged ship commits are not credited to MILESTONE_PROGRESS; reconcile via close-out-milestone.mjs, do not trust shipped:0.
A coordinator is pure orchestration — it should hold no domain logic; keep it a thin sequencer (R8 — read the sibling units, do not reimplement them).

AUTO-LEARNING-LOOP-MS0::U-ALL02.systemImpact: NoveltyDetectionEngine diffs new programs against the catalog; it is the front gate of the AUTO-LEARNING-LOOP — only novel items proceed to learning. A false positive (flagging a re-ordered duplicate as new) wastes the token budget; a false negative (missing genuine novelty) starves the learning loop. The weekly review surface (U-ALL10) consumes its output.
csDepth: Hash-normalize entries before diffing — content hashing must canonicalize ordering (sort keys, normalize whitespace) so a re-ordered-but-identical item hashes equal; a naive hash flags every reorder as novel.
Set-difference against a reference catalog is O(n) with a hash set; the catalog hash set must be kept current — a stale catalog mis-classifies recently-added items as novel.

AUTO-LEARNING-LOOP-MS0::U-ALL05.systemImpact: VizAutoAugmentationEngine emits a system-viz ghost-roost augmentation file; it must be registered in BOTH regen-viz.mjs FAST[] AND the merge-augmentations splice — one without the other silently drops the roost from /system-viz. The system-graph.json has multiple writers, so the augmentation write is a known race surface.
csDepth: Atomic file write (temp + rename) is mandatory — system-graph.json has three independent writers and a non-atomic augmentation write can be read mid-write as truncated JSON.
Idempotent regeneration: re-emitting the augmentation must not append duplicate ghost nodes — dedupe by stable node id before splice.

AUTO-LEARNING-LOOP-MS0::U-ALL07.systemImpact: Wiring the 6 auto-learning actions to devDispatcher makes the AUTO-LEARNING-LOOP-MS0 capabilities reachable; the cron registration (U-ALL09) invokes these actions on schedule, so a ghost-wire makes the scheduled learning loop a no-op that reports success.
csDepth: Each of the 6 actions must be in the z.enum() gate with a real executor — verify each one round-trips; partial wiring (4 of 6) leaves the loop incomplete.
Auto-learning actions mutate persistent state — the dispatcher contract must serialize concurrent invocations of the same action or two cron fires race the learning ledger.

AUTO-LEARNING-LOOP-MS0::U-ALL08.systemImpact: U-ALL08 is the second wiring unit for the auto-learning actions (paired with U-ALL07); together they complete the 6-action surface that the cron schedule and the weekly review surface depend on. Incomplete wiring here breaks the closed-loop learning pipeline downstream.
csDepth: Wiring is incomplete unless each action is in the enum gate with a real executor and a passing round-trip E2E — a mock that skips z.enum() false-greens a missing action.
Verify the 6 actions across U-ALL07 + U-ALL08 are disjoint and exhaustive — overlapping or missing actions between the two units leave a gap or a duplicate-route hazard.

AUTO-LEARNING-LOOP-MS0::U-ALL09.systemImpact: The 6 cron entries drive the AUTO-LEARNING-LOOP on schedule; idempotent registration is critical — re-running the registrar must not add 6 duplicate cron entries, which would fire the learning loop 2x and double the token spend that U-ALL11's budget guard must then absorb.
csDepth: Idempotent registration: check existing cron entries by a stable key before appending — a non-idempotent registrar accumulates duplicates on every re-run.
Off-peak minute selection avoids fleet-wide cron pile-up — every job at minute 0 lands simultaneously; stagger to off-:00/:30 minutes (the documented cron-fleet pattern).

AUTO-LEARNING-LOOP-MS0::U-ALL10.systemImpact: The weekly human-in-loop review surface is the safety gate of the entire AUTO-LEARNING-LOOP — it presents NoveltyDetectionEngine's diffs for explicit approval; no learned change reaches the catalog without passing through it. If it auto-applies, the loop becomes an unsupervised self-modification path.
csDepth: The review surface must present concrete diffs for human approval — never auto-apply learned changes; the approve/reject gate is the only thing separating closed-loop learning from uncontrolled drift.
Approve/reject is a state machine — model pending/approved/rejected/expired explicitly; an item with no terminal state silently lingers in the queue forever.

AUTO-LEARNING-LOOP-MS0::U-ALL11.systemImpact: The 12/day, $20/day token-budget guard is the cost ceiling of the AUTO-LEARNING-LOOP; if it fails open, the cron-driven loop (U-ALL09) can spiral unbounded token spend. Every auto-learning action (U-ALL07/08) should check the guard before running.
csDepth: The budget ledger is a concurrent read-modify-write target — multiple cron fires racing the ledger can both see 'under budget' and both spend; use an atomic RMW (lockfile or compare-and-swap), not naive read-then-write.

Fail closed when over budget — the guard must DENY when the ledger says over, never push through (R6 — token budgets are not advisory); also handle the daily-reset boundary correctly so a stale day's count does not leak.

AUTO-LEARNING-LOOP-MS0::U-ALL12.systemImpact: The source-poisoning sanitizer is the security gate of the AUTO-LEARNING-LOOP — every learned source passes through it before ingest. An unvalidated source poisons the whole loop: a prompt-injection payload in a learned source can corrupt every downstream model and the catalog. This is the loop's trust boundary.
csDepth: Allowlist-based validation is fail-closed by construction — only allowlisted sources pass; an unknown source is rejected, never default-allowed.
SHA-256 content hashing provides provenance — pin the hash of an approved source so a later silent content change is detected; prompt-injection detection must scan content, not just the source URL.

AWARE-MS0::U-AWARE01.systemImpact: The build/create-detection PreToolUse hook is the trigger for the whole self-awareness gate stack — inventory-check-guard, master-index-search-gate, dedup-auto-invoke, and duplication-hard-block all key off detecting build intent. If it mis-classifies, the entire mandatory-self-awareness chain either over-fires (noise) or silently fails to fire (duplicate engines ship).
csDepth: Keyword classification must strip quoted regions before matching — a build/create word inside a quoted string or a comment is not build intent; the documented magic-number-scan and stopword fixes apply here.
Exit 0 and emit decisions via stdout JSON — exit-2 truncates the stdout pipe on Windows and silently bypasses the gate (the recurring hook-contract bug).

AWARE-MS0::U-AWARE03.systemImpact: The master-index search gate runs a graph keyword search on every build-intent prompt; if it OOMs on the ~370MB system-graph.json it silently disables the gate fleet-wide, so duplicate engines slip past. The master-index-filter-contract-fix wiki documents the min_confidence post-blend filter bug that affects ranking here.
csDepth: Cap graph-file size BEFORE JSON.parse — the documented 200MB/80MB caps exist because the full graph OOMs the hook; an OOM kills the gate silently (the F1 silent-degrade class).

BM25 / inverted-index ranking over graph nodes — the min_confidence filter must apply POST-blend (after the confidence × utilization-floor blend), not pre-blend, or the user sees a score below the threshold they filtered on.

AWARE-MS0::U-AWARE05.systemImpact: Auto-/dedup invocation runs DuplicationGuardEngine silently on build intent; it is the soft-warning tier ahead of the duplication-hard-block (U-AWARE07). A false positive that surfaces noisily annoys every chat; a false negative lets a duplicate engine reach the hard-block or, worse, ship.
csDepth: Fuzzy similarity matching (keyword overlap) needs a calibrated threshold — too loose floods false matches, too tight misses near-duplicates; the soft tier should err toward surfacing, the hard-block toward exactness.
Auto-invocation must be silent on no-match and exit 0 always — signal via stdout, never block on a fuzzy match (only the hard-block blocks).

AWARE-MS0::U-AWARE06.systemImpact: AI feature recommendation injection surfaces relevant engines via UserPromptSubmit additionalContext; it depends on AICapabilityMaximizerEngine's recommendations. Unconditional injection burns the token budget on every prompt — it must be keyword-gated and relevance-ranked, and the loop-inject-dedup gate suppresses byte-identical re-injection across /loop iterations.
csDepth: Inject on relevance only via hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext — a noisy unconditional injection is a per-prompt token tax (the loop-inject cost-audit measured ~518 tok/iter of stable-redundant inject).
Relevance ranking over recommendations is a top-K selection — bound K small; an unbounded recommendation list defeats the purpose of a focused injection.

AWARE-MS0::U-AWARE07.systemImpact: The duplication hard-block is the terminal gate of the self-awareness stack — it DENIES creation of an exact-duplicate engine via PreToolUse. A false hard-block stalls every chat trying to do legitimate work; a missed block lets a true duplicate ship and fragment the codebase. duplicationGuardEngine.mustCheckBeforeCreating throws to back it.
csDepth: Block ONLY on an EXACT duplicate (name + keyword match) — a fuzzy match must route to the soft tier (U-AWARE05), never the hard-block; a false hard-block is a fleet-wide stall.
Hard-block via stdout JSON deny decision with exit 0 — exit-2 truncates the pipe and the block silently does not fire, which is the worst failure mode for a guard.

AWARE-MS0::U-AWARE08.systemImpact: The AWARE-MS0 test suite is the regression oracle for the self-awareness hook stack; if the hook contracts (build-create-detector, search-gate, dedup, hard-block) are not covered with real-value tests, a silent hook regression disables the whole mandatory-self-awareness layer without anyone noticing.
csDepth: Hook tests must drive the real stdin/stdout JSON contract via subprocess fixtures — a pure-function test of the classifier misses the exit-code and pipe-truncation behavior where the bugs actually live.
Tests must encode why behavior matters with real values, and the change must reflect across all four doc surfaces in the same session — a hook documented in only one surface rots.

BENCH-MS0::P0-U00.systemImpact: BenchmarkSuiteEngine is the core infrastructure for BENCH-MS0; the sibling units (P0-U06 geometries, P0-U07 parametric sweep) plug fixtures and scenarios into it. A benchmark-suite harness needs a fixture/scenario registry that is deterministic and content-addressable so benchmark runs are reproducible across sessions.

BENCH-MS0::P0-U07.systemImpact: The 8,640-combination parametric sweep stresses AutoSpeedFeedCalculatorEngine across the full speed/feed grid; its results are the benchmark dataset BenchmarkSuiteEngine reports. A sweep that OOMs or writes non-atomically corrupts the benchmark output that BENCH-MS0 closeout depends on.
csDepth: An 8,640-combination Cartesian product must be a bounded, lazy enumeration — materializing all 8,640 result objects in memory before write risks OOM; stream and write atomically per chunk.
Each combination's speed/feed result is bounded by canonical Kienzle/Taylor physics — the sweep must import constants from constants.ts so the benchmark grid is anchored to the canonical envelope.

BIZ-MS2::U-BIZ17.systemImpact: The timecard audit trail is the SOX/ISO compliance record for BIZ-MS2; the HR audit viewer reads it and BIZ-MS5's AS9100 audit manager shares the append-only-ledger pattern. Tamper-evidence via hash chaining: each entry hashes the previous entry's hash — a single altered record breaks the chain and is detectable; this is the SOX requirement, not optional.

BIZ-MS5::U-BIZ41.systemImpact: The ISO/AS9100 audit manager tracks compliance findings as an append-only ledger; it shares the ledger-store/projector pattern with BIZ-MS2's timecard trail and the OSHA compliance engine. A silently-dropped non-conformance is an audit failure with legal exposure — every finding must be a durable ledger entry.
csDepth: The compliance lifecycle is a state machine (open → in-review → closed/non-conformance) — model every state explicitly; a finding with no terminal state is a silently-dropped non-conformance.
ISO/AS9100 clause-to-control mapping is a many-to-many relation — a control may satisfy multiple clauses; store the mapping explicitly so a control change re-evaluates every affected clause.

BOX-AUDIT::U-BOXX01.systemImpact: The BOX-AUDIT coordinator sequences the box-program audit sub-units; it closes the milestone only when each box-program deliverable exists on disk. A premature close records box-audit work as complete in MILESTONE_PROGRESS when the box programs were never converted — the silent-close-out-debt class.
csDepth: Verify each box-program deliverable exists on disk before closing — file presence is necessary but not sufficient; the close-out-audit is advisory and every candidate must be human-verified.

Batch macro conversion across box programs is an embarrassingly-parallel workload — but the coordinator must aggregate per-program success/failure honestly; one failed conversion in a batch is a milestone-incomplete signal.

BP-MS0::U-APPR2.systemImpact: The timeline + comments + attachments record is the event-stream substrate for the BP-MS0 approval workflow; it is built on the ledger-store/projector. Other BP-MS0 units project the approval state from this event stream — if an event write is lost or non-atomic, the projected approval state diverges from reality.
csDepth: An append-only timeline is an event-sourced log — the current approval state is a projection over the event stream; never mutate a past event, append a correcting one.

Attachments must be keyed to a STABLE record id, not an array index — a re-ordered timeline would otherwise orphan attachments; write each event atomically so a crash mid-write does not leave a partial event.

CAD-AUTOMATION-MS0::U-CAUT01.systemImpact: CADInstallationProbeEngine is the first stage of CAD-AUTOMATION-MS0 — every bridge (U-CAUT02..07) and the router (U-CAUT10) keys off which CAD software it reports as installed. If it throws when software is absent rather than returning not-installed, the whole automation dispatcher fails to initialize on a machine missing one CAD package.
csDepth: Windows registry probing must fail soft — a missing registry key is the expected 'not installed' case, not an exception; return a structured not-installed result, never throw (R12 honest, but soft for an expected-absent case).
Registry + filesystem path discovery should cross-check — a registry entry without a resolvable install path means a broken/uninstalled package; report that distinctly from cleanly-absent.

CAD-AUTOMATION-MS0::U-CAUT02.systemImpact: SolidWorksAutomationBridge is the COM access path consumed by CADAutomationRouter (U-CAUT10) for .sldprt/.sldasm/.slddrw files; it sets the COM-lifecycle convention that the Inventor bridge (U-CAUT03) explicitly mirrors. csDepth: COM/IDispatch interop must release every reference deterministically — a leaked COM object keeps the SolidWorks process alive; use a try/finally release pattern, not GC-dependent cleanup.
COM HRESULT failures must be surfaced loudly with the HRESULT code — a swallowed COM error looks like a clean no-op but left a wedged process.

CAD-AUTOMATION-MS0::U-CAUT03.systemImpact: InventorAutomationBridge is the COM path for .ipt/.iam/.idw consumed by CADAutomationRouter; it must match the SolidWorks bridge's COM lifecycle convention (U-CAUT02) so the router treats both uniformly. The cad-fusion-training-ms0 wiki notes Inventor/STEP is the transferable corpus when Fusion cloud is unreachable — this bridge is on that path.
csDepth: Match the SolidWorks bridge's COM lifecycle convention — divergent COM cleanup between two bridges makes the router's process management inconsistent and one bridge will leak.
Inventor's .iam assembly model loads referenced .ipt files lazily — the bridge must handle a missing referenced part gracefully, not crash the whole assembly open.

CAD-AUTOMATION-MS0::U-CAUT04.systemImpact: FreeCADAutomationBridge spawns a Python subprocess for .FCStd access; it is consumed by CADAutomationRouter and its orphan-Python processes are exactly what CADProcessSpawner (U-CAUT08) and the fleet-reaper must clean up. A hung FreeCAD parse with no timeout accumulates orphans that OOM the host.
csDepth: Subprocess spawn must set a hard timeout and capture stderr — a .FCStd parse that hangs with no timeout leaves an orphan Python process; kill it on timeout, do not wait indefinitely.
stdin/stdout IPC with the FreeCAD process needs a framed protocol (length-prefixed or delimiter) — raw stream parsing can fuse two messages or split one across reads.

CAD-AUTOMATION-MS0::U-CAUT05.systemImpact: MastercamAutomationBridge is the .NET-hook path for .mcx*/.mcam consumed by CADAutomationRouter; Mastercam is the most-used CAM vendor, so this bridge is high-traffic. A .NET exception swallowed at the cross-language boundary looks like a clean failure but left a wedged addin host the fleet-reaper must reap.
csDepth: Surface .NET exceptions across the process boundary loudly — a cross-language IPC boundary swallows exceptions easily; serialize the .NET exception type and message back to the Node caller.
Verify the .NET addin host process exits cleanly after each operation — a host that lingers is an orphan; track its PID with CADProcessSpawner.

CAD-AUTOMATION-MS0::U-CAUT06.systemImpact: Fusion360AutomationBridge is the HTTP-bridge path for .f3d/.f3z consumed by CADAutomationRouter; the cad-fusion-training-ms0 wiki documents that Fusion cloud is unreachable without Forge creds, so this bridge must degrade gracefully when the local server is down rather than blocking the whole router.
csDepth: Handle connection-refused explicitly — the Fusion HTTP bridge server may not be started; never assume the local server is up, set a request timeout, and report bridge-unavailable distinctly from a parse failure.
An HTTP bridge needs idempotent retry on transient connection errors but NOT on a 4xx — distinguish a not-started server (retry) from a bad request (fail fast).

CAD-AUTOMATION-MS0::U-CAUT07.systemImpact: HyperMILLAutomationBridge is the AC-Python path for .hmc consumed by CADAutomationRouter; like the FreeCAD bridge it spawns an interpreter subprocess whose orphans the CADProcessSpawner and fleet-reaper must reap. hyperMILL has 25 already-extracted assets — the bridge reads existing files, no re-extraction.
csDepth: AC Python automation spawns an interpreter subprocess — set a timeout, capture stderr, and reap the orphan on a hung .hmc operation; match the FreeCAD bridge's subprocess lifecycle convention.
Subprocess timeout handling must distinguish a slow-but-progressing operation from a true hang — a fixed timeout that is too short kills a large legitimate .hmc file.

CAD-AUTOMATION-MS0::U-CAUT08.systemImpact: CADProcessSpawner is the shared subprocess-lifecycle manager that every CAD bridge (U-CAUT02..07) routes its spawns through; it is the single chokepoint preventing CAD-process orphan accumulation. If it leaks a PID, the fleet-reaper's slot-attribution layer is the only backstop, and a leaked CAD process can OOM the memory-pressured host.
csDepth: Track every spawned PID in a registry and reap on timeout/crash — a leaked CAD process accumulates; this is the same orphan class the fleet-reaper handles, so the spawner should be the first line of defense.
PID tracking has a reuse hazard — the OS recycles PIDs; track spawn time alongside PID so a recycled PID is not mistaken for the original process (the fleet-reaper PID-reuse edge case).

CAD-AUTOMATION-MS0::U-CAUT09.systemImpact: CADAutomationMockLayer provides deterministic fixtures so CAD-AUTOMATION-MS0's CI runs without real CAD software installed; if the mock fabricates a response shape the real bridge never emits, every CI test false-greens and a production bridge bug ships. This is the documented 'hermetic fakes don't prove wiring' hazard.

Dependency injection for the bridge layer lets CI swap the mock in — but the suite must ALSO ship at least one real-bridge E2E (gated on software presence) so the mock-vs-real divergence is caught.

An unhandled file extension that silently no-ops, rather than failing loud, makes the dispatcher return empty for a whole CAD format class.
csDepth: The format→bridge dispatch table (strategy pattern) must be explicit and exhaustive — fail loud on an unknown extension; a default-case that silently returns empty hides an unsupported-format bug.
The router should consult CADInstallationProbeEngine — routing a .sldprt to the SolidWorks bridge is futile if SolidWorks is not installed; surface installed-but-absent distinctly.

CAD-AUTOMATION-MS0::U-CAUT11.systemImpact: CADAutomationDispatcher is the MCP surface for CAD-AUTOMATION-MS0 — it exposes the router (U-CAUT10) and bridges as dispatcher actions; an enum-only ghost-wire makes the whole CAD-automation capability unreachable from the MCP surface and stop_on_unwired_assets blocks the Stop. The 30-file smoke test (U-CAUT12) drives this dispatcher.

Zod validation at the MCP boundary must match the router's actual input shape — read the router signature before authoring the schema (schema-blindness).

CAD-AUTOMATION-MS0::U-CAUT12.systemImpact: The 30-file multi-format smoke test is the integration regression oracle for the whole CAD-AUTOMATION-MS0 milestone — it drives the real router + bridges + dispatcher end to end. If it runs only hermetic mocks, a production bridge or router bug ships green; it must include at least one real-file E2E.
csDepth: A smoke test must drive the REAL router + bridges, not only the mock layer — at least one real-file E2E per format, gated on software presence, is the only thing that proves the mock matches the producer.
A 30-file sweep is a fixture-management problem — store fixtures content-addressably and assert concrete per-file results, not just 'no exception thrown' (R9).

CAD-COMPLETE-MS0::U-CADC23.systemImpact: U-CADC23 is a CAD-COMPLETE-MS0 geometry unit reconciling a feature-gap-audit finding; its CAD-generation output feeds cadDispatcher and is consumed by downstream CAM toolpath generation. CAD-COMPLETE-MS0::U-CADC32.systemImpact: U-CADC32 is a CAD-COMPLETE-MS0 geometry unit; its output feeds cadDispatcher CAD-generation and the CAD↔CAM bridge. CAD-COMPLETE-MS0 collectively must land for the cad-fusion geometry model to be auto-wired into build-sequence inference (the documented open gap).

CAD-COMPLETE-MS0::U-CADC33.systemImpact: U-CADC33 is a CAD-COMPLETE-MS0 geometry unit; its CAD-generation output is consumed by cadDispatcher and the print-to-program GEOMETRY_PARSE / FEATURE_RECOG stages. CAD-COMPLETE-MS0::U-CADC41.systemImpact: U-CADC41 is a CAD-COMPLETE-MS0 geometry unit; its output feeds cadDispatcher CAD-generation and build-sequence inference. CAD-COMPLETE-MS0 units collectively gate the CAD half of the print-to-program pipeline (INPUT_HALF for the cad domain).
csDepth: Verify the gap is real before porting — Glob engines/cad; the FEATURE-GAP-AUDIT lesson is that most 'digest=0 absent' units are stale-digest false-positives.
Build-sequence inference may need to handle ambiguous orderings — when two features have no dependency between them, pick a deterministic canonical order so the inferred sequence is reproducible.

CAD-COMPLETE-MS0::U-CADC42.systemImpact: U-CADC42 is a CAD-COMPLETE-MS0 geometry unit; its CAD-generation output is consumed by cadDispatcher and the CAD↔CAM AI bridge. A geometry regression here ships wrong feature trees into CAM toolpath generation downstream.
csDepth: Glob the engines tree before porting — verify the gap is real, not a stale digest flag (the recurring false-positive class).

CAD-COMPLETE-MS0::U-CADC35.systemImpact: U-CADC35 is a CAD-COMPLETE-MS0 geometry unit (unit 1 of the milestone); its output feeds cadDispatcher CAD-generation and the print-to-program GEOMETRY_PARSE stage. As an early unit it may set conventions the later CADC units (22/23/32/33/41/42) follow.
